To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the majority (56 %) of miRNAs detected are differentially localized in nuclear and cytosolic compartments and that the hypoxic response is accompanied by changes in miRNA expression in each of the compartments.

(1) a large population of nuclear miRNAs is differentially regulated by hypoxia and (2) the majority of hypoxia-regulated miRNAs are differentially expressed between the nuclear and cytoplamic compartments.
hypoxia induces widespread differential miRNA distribution between nuclear and cytoplamic compartments in a mouse endothelium cell line.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of novel nuclear miRNA functions in the hypoxamiR response.
the role of small RNA species in the regulation of gene expression in the nucleus.
understanding the role of microRNAs in the regulation of cellular processes and the development of novel therapeutics for the treatment of ischemic diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
miRNAs have been found to have nuclear functions, and these functions are regulated in response to hypothermia.
hypoxic stress induces changes in the distribution of miRNAs between nuclear and cytoplamsic compartments.
miRNAs are highly abundant, diverse, and differentially expressed in both nuclear and cellular compartments, and are regulated by hypoxia in a compartment-specific manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nuclear and cytoplamic miRNA pools are differentially regulated in response to hypoxide stress, and this is likely to contribute to the overall cellular response.
hypoxia is a powerful regulator of nuclear and cytoplamic miRNA distribution.
hypoxia induces a widespread change in the nuclear miRNA landscape, and that the nuclear compartment is a key site for miRNA-mediated gene regulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cell nucleus is not a static compartment but is rather an active participant in the cellular response to hypoxic stimulus.
the nuclear and cytoplamic miRNA populations are not simply a subset of each other, but rather are highly distinct and differentially regulated.
miRNAs are highly dynamic and compartment-specific molecules.
